title: Efficiency of the composite verifier
statement: For Boolean strings $x$ and $r$, interpret each string as a nonnegative integer by reading its bits in the order in which they occur, with the first bit having weight $1$. The composite verifier accepts automatically when the integer represented by $x$ is less than $2$, rejects when it equals $2$, and accepts when it is even. Otherwise it rejects exactly when two successive Euler-liar rounds, each using $|x|+3$ bits of $r$ per round, both identify the sampled value as an Euler liar for the integer represented by $x$. This verifier, viewed as returning its Boolean decision as an optional Boolean value, is efficient in the polynomial-time verifier model.
caveat: The supplied statement does not define the verifier model or its efficiency predicate. The acceptance description follows the provided definitions of the composite verifier and its two Euler-liar rounds.
